chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from more than one, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimi, from Harun ibn Harizah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you desire a matter, take six pieces of paper and write on three of them: 'In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. A choice from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. For So-and-so ibn So-and-so, do it.' And on the other three: 'In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. A choice from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. For So-and-so ibn So-and-so, do not do it.' Then place them beneath your prayer mat. When you finish, prostrate and say one hundred times: 'I seek Allah's choice through His mercy, a choice in well-being.' Then sit upright and say: 'O Allah, choose for me in all my affairs with ease from You and well-being.' Then strike with your hand towards the papers, mix them, and draw out one. If three consecutive ones are 'do it', then do that matter which you intend. And if three consecutive ones are 'do not do it', then do not do it. And if one is 'do it' and the other is 'do not do it', then draw out from the papers up to five, and look at the majority, and act according to it, and leave the sixth, for you do not need it.
ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step method for performing Istikhara using written slips according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific ritual of Istikhara using written slips (qur'ah), reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of combining supplication with a tangible method of divination to seek divine guidance. It emphasizes the integration of physical action—placing slips under the prayer mat and drawing lots—with spiritual devotion, specifically reciting 'Astakhirullah' one hundred times in prostration. This practice underscores the belief that while human effort is required, the ultimate outcome is determined by Allah's wisdom and choice.
